summary: AtomVecKokkos_PackBorderVel drops the non-deform-group velocity branch, so with fix deform + remap v the buffer is short by 3 doubles for every atom outside the deform group and every field packed after v lands at the wrong offset.
failure_scenario: atom_style sphere/kk (or any kk style) + 'fix deform ... remap v' + 'comm_modify vel yes' on a GPU build (forward/exchange comm on device): border atoms not in the deform group get an uninitialized/garbage ghost velocity and every following border-vel field (radius, rmass, omega, q, molecule, mu, angmom, DPD energies) is read from the wrong buffer slot -> wrong forces/energies, potentially NaN.
suggested_fix: Add the missing else branch that writes _v(j,0..2) unshifted (and advances m) when the atom is not in the deform group, exactly as src/atom_vec.cpp:955-959 does.

summary: AtomVecKokkos_PackCommVel never initializes its _mu and _sp views, yet operator() reads them when datamask_comm_vel carries MU_MASK/SP_MASK (atom_style dipole/kk, spin/kk), dereferencing a default-constructed (null) Kokkos view.
failure_scenario: 'atom_style dipole/kk' with 'comm_modify vel yes' on a GPU build -> pack_comm_vel_kokkos launches a kernel that reads _mu(j,0) from an unallocated view: segfault/illegal memory access (or silent garbage dipoles on ghosts with bounds checking off).
suggested_fix: Add _mu(atomKK->k_mu.view<DeviceType>()) and _sp(atomKK->k_sp.view<DeviceType>()) to the AtomVecKokkos_PackCommVel initializer list, in member-declaration order.

summary: unpack_border_vel_kokkos picks the 'x/tag/type/mask/v only' functor based on ncomm_vel instead of nborder_vel, so for atom_style charge/bond/angle/molecular/full the q and molecule values that pack_border_vel_kokkos wrote are never unpacked into ghost atoms.
failure_scenario: 'atom_style full/kk' + 'comm_modify vel yes' (e.g. with fix rigid or a granular/SPH pair style) on a GPU build: every ghost atom keeps a stale or uninitialized charge and molecule ID after each reneighboring -> wrong Coulomb forces and wrong special-bond/molecule-ID-based exclusions.
suggested_fix: Branch on `!nborder_vel` (not `!ncomm_vel`) in unpack_border_vel_kokkos, or give AtomVecKokkos_PackBorderVel the same DEFAULT template parameter so packer and unpacker are selected by the same predicate.

summary: field2size("num_improper") sizes the improper block with atom->dihedral_per_atom instead of atom->improper_per_atom, so size_exchange is too small whenever a system has more impropers per atom than dihedrals per atom, and pack_exchange writes past the end of its buffer row.
failure_scenario: atom_style full/kk or molecular/kk for a molecule with e.g. improper_per_atom=6 and dihedral_per_atom=4: pack_exchange_kokkos writes 10 doubles past the row for every migrating atom, corrupting the next atom's exchange record (and the last row overruns the allocation) -> lost/garbled bonded topology or a crash during atom migration.
suggested_fix: Return 1+5*atom->improper_per_atom for the "num_improper" field.

summary: None of the forward-comm functors handle RADIUS_MASK/RMASS_MASK, so 'atom_style sphere/kk 1' (dynamic radii) silently never forward-communicates radius and rmass to ghost atoms even though size_forward reserves room for them.
failure_scenario: 'atom_style sphere/kk 1' with 'fix adapt ... diameter' on a GPU build: ghost particles keep their radius and rmass from the last borders() call, so pair granular/gran overlap distances and masses are wrong for every ghost contact -> wrong forces, silently.
suggested_fix: Add `if (_datamask & RADIUS_MASK) ...` and `if (_datamask & RMASS_MASK) ...` blocks (in the order used by pack_border) to AtomVecKokkos_PackComm, UnpackComm, PackCommSelf, PackCommSelfFused, PackCommVel and UnpackCommVel, or reject radvary in AtomVecSphereKokkos.

summary: AtomVecKokkos::~AtomVecKokkos never frees the pinned staging buffer allocated by perform_pinned_copy/perform_pinned_copy_transform, leaking it for the lifetime of the process.
failure_scenario: An input script that changes atom_style (or any run that constructs and destroys several LAMMPS instances / uses the library interface repeatedly) leaks nmax*3*sizeof(double) of page-locked host memory per atom_vec instance; pinned memory is a scarce resource and exhausting it makes further CUDA/HIP allocations fail.
suggested_fix: In ~AtomVecKokkos, `if (buffer) Kokkos::kokkos_free<LMPPinnedHostType>(buffer);` (guarded by the same #ifdef LMP_KOKKOS_GPU as the allocation) and reset buffer/buffer_size.

summary: set_atom_masks compares a signed int loop index against std::vector::size(), producing sign-compare warnings in every one of its seven loops.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/atom_vec_kokkos.cpp:2976, 2982, 2988, 2994, 3000, 3006, 3012 all read `for (int i = 0; i < default_xxx.size(); i++)` where default_xxx is a `const std::vector<std::string>` (src/atom_vec.cpp:33-41).  set_size_exchange has the same pattern at line 3023.
failure_scenario: No runtime defect; -Wsign-compare noise that can hide real warnings during the release build.
suggested_fix: Use `std::size_t i` (or a range-for over the vector) in these loops.

verified_by: orchestrator (read code directly; found by group 02)
summary: AtomVecKokkos_PackBorderVel: under DEFORM_VREMAP only atoms in the deform group get their velocity packed (no else branch), so every other atom's border-with-velocity record is 3 doubles short and all later fields are misaligned with the unpacker, which always reads 3 velocity slots.
evidence: atom_vec_kokkos.cpp:1848-1858 vs src/atom_vec.cpp pack_border_vel which has the else branch writing v unshifted.
failure_scenario: 'fix deform ... remap v' + 'comm_modify vel yes' on a GPU: ghost velocities and every following border field (radius, rmass, omega, q, molecule, ...) read from the wrong buffer slot.
suggested_fix: Add the missing else branch writing _v(j,0..2).

verified_by: orchestrator (read code directly; found by group 02)
summary: AtomVecKokkos_PackCommVel never initializes its _mu and _sp view members although operator() reads them under MU_MASK/SP_MASK (dipole/kk, spin/kk).
evidence: members declared at 788-789; constructor initializer list 809-822 lacks them; sibling PackComm/UnpackCommVel initialize both.
failure_scenario: atom_style dipole/kk or spin/kk with comm_modify vel yes on a GPU: kernel dereferences an empty view (illegal memory access or garbage ghost dipoles/spins).
suggested_fix: Initialize _mu(atomKK->k_mu.view<DeviceType>()) and _sp(atomKK->k_sp.view<DeviceType>()).

verified_by: orchestrator (read code directly; found by group 02)
summary: unpack_border_vel_kokkos selects the reduced (x/tag/type/mask/v only) functor on '!ncomm_vel' while the packer packs whatever datamask_border_vel says; styles with border-only extra fields (charge, bond, angle, molecular, full: q and molecule) have ncomm_vel==0 and nborder_vel>0, so q/molecule are packed but never unpacked into ghosts.
evidence: atom_vec_kokkos.cpp:2131/2145 '!ncomm_vel'; the non-vel path at 1575/1741 branches on '!nborder'. src/atom_vec_charge.cpp fields_border_vel={q}, no fields_comm_vel.
failure_scenario: atom_style full/kk + comm_modify vel yes on a GPU: ghosts keep stale charge and molecule ID after each reneighbor -> wrong Coulomb forces and exclusions.
suggested_fix: Branch on !nborder_vel (or give the packer the same DEFAULT template parameter).

verified_by: orchestrator (read code directly; found by group 02)
summary: field2size("num_improper") returns 1+5*atom->dihedral_per_atom instead of improper_per_atom, so the exchange buffer row is too small whenever improper_per_atom > dihedral_per_atom.
evidence: atom_vec_kokkos.cpp:2955-2956.
failure_scenario: full/kk or molecular/kk with more impropers than dihedrals per atom: pack_exchange_kokkos writes past the row for every migrating atom -> corrupted topology or crash during migration.
suggested_fix: Use atom->improper_per_atom.

verified_by: orchestrator (read code directly; found by group 02)
summary: None of the forward-comm functors (PackComm, UnpackComm, PackCommSelf, PackCommSelfFused, PackCommVel, UnpackCommVel) handle RADIUS_MASK/RMASS_MASK, so 'atom_style sphere/kk 1' (dynamic radius; fields_comm = radius,rmass) never forward-communicates radius and mass to ghosts even though size_forward reserves room for them.
evidence: grep RADIUS_MASK atom_vec_kokkos.cpp: hits only in border/exchange functors (lines 1534+), none in the forward comm functors (80-1140). src/atom_vec_sphere.cpp:68-70 sets fields_comm={radius,rmass} when radvary.
failure_scenario: sphere/kk 1 with fix adapt diameter on a GPU: ghost radii/masses stale since the last borders() -> wrong granular contacts, silently.
suggested_fix: Add RADIUS/RMASS branches to the six forward-comm functors in the same order pack_border uses, or reject radvary in AtomVecSphereKokkos.

summary: init_one() fills only the (i,j) element of the self-allocated k_cut_ljsq/k_cut_coulsq dual views, leaving (j,i) at zero, so with more than MAX_TYPES_STACKPARAMS (12) atom types every pair with itype>jtype loses its entire Coulomb interaction.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/pair_coul_cut_kokkos.cpp:181-184 allocates standalone views 'k_cut_ljsq = DAT::tdual_kkfloat_2d("pair:cut_ljsq",n+1,n+1);' / 'k_cut_coulsq = DAT::tdual_kkfloat_2d(...)' (NOT aliased to any host array), and :230/:232 write only 'k_cut_ljsq.view_host()(i,j) = ...' / 'k_cut_coulsq.view_host()(i,j) = ...' while init_one is only called with i<=j (src/pair.cpp:284-288).  The functor uses these for the non-stack path: src/KOKKOS/pair_kokkos.h:245-249 'if (rsq < (STACKPARAMS?c.m_cut_ljsq[itype][jtype]:c.d_cut_ljsq(itype,jtype)))' and 'if (rsq < (STACKPARAMS?c.m_cut_coulsq[itype][jtype]:c.d_cut_coulsq(itype,jtype)))', and pair_kokkos.h:955/969 select STACKPARAMS=false when 'fpair->atom->ntypes > MAX_TYPES_STACKPARAMS' (=12, kokkos_type.h:44).  Sibling styles do it correctly, e.g. src/KOKKOS/pair_coul_cut_soft_kokkos.cpp:232-234 'k_cut_ljsq.view_host()(i,j) = k_cut_ljsq.view_host()(j,i) = ...'.
failure_scenario: pair_style coul/cut/kk with 13 or more atom types: for a neighbor pair with itype=5, jtype=3 the test 'rsq < d_cut_coulsq(5,3)' compares against 0, compute_fcoul/compute_ecoul are never called, and the Coulomb force and energy of that pair are silently zero (roughly half of all cross-type interactions).
suggested_fix: Write both elements in init_one, i.e. 'k_cut_ljsq.view_host()(i,j) = k_cut_ljsq.view_host()(j,i) = cutone*cutone;' and the same for k_cut_coulsq.

summary: compute() never sets copymode = 1 around the pair_compute<> call, unlike every other pair style in the package.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/pair_coul_cut_kokkos.cpp:106-113 goes straight from 'qqrd2e = ...' to 'EV_FLOAT ev = pair_compute<PairCoulCutKokkos<DeviceType>,void >(this,...)' with no 'copymode = 1;' / 'copymode = 0;'; compare src/KOKKOS/pair_buck_coul_cut_kokkos.cpp:121-151.  Same omission in pair_coul_debye_kokkos.cpp, pair_coul_cut_soft_kokkos.cpp and pair_coul_long_soft_kokkos.cpp.
failure_scenario: Currently benign because ~PairComputeFunctor (src/KOKKOS/pair_kokkos.h:103) sets c.copymode = 1 on its own copy before destruction; but any future code path that copies the style outside the functor would double-free the Kokkos/host arrays.
suggested_fix: Add 'copymode = 1;' before the pair_compute<> call and 'copymode = 0;' at the end of compute(), matching the rest of the package.

summary: init_one() fills only the (i,j) element of the standalone k_cut_ljsq/k_cut_coulsq dual views (init_one is called with i<=j only), so with more than MAX_TYPES_STACKPARAMS=12 atom types the non-stack path tests rsq against 0 for every itype>jtype pair and drops the Coulomb interaction entirely. Same defect in pair_coul_debye_kokkos.cpp:253.
verified_by: orchestrator (src/KOKKOS/pair_coul_cut_kokkos.cpp:230-233 and pair_coul_debye_kokkos.cpp:253-256 assign only (i,j); the stack copies m_cut_ljsq/m_cut_coulsq right above DO set [j][i]. The correct sibling is pair_coul_cut_soft_kokkos.cpp:232-234, which assigns (i,j) and (j,i). k_cutsq itself is safe because it is aliased to the base cutsq array that Pair::init symmetrizes at src/pair.cpp:288.)

summary: FixNVESphereKokkos ignores the 'update dipole/dlm' option: it always applies the simple cross-product dipole integrator, so 'fix nve/sphere/kk ... update dipole/dlm' silently uses a different (non-symplectic) integrator than the CPU style and never updates omega.
failure_scenario: 'fix 1 all nve/sphere/kk update dipole/dlm' on a dipolar sphere system: the run silently uses the plain cross-product update (and never rotates omega), giving a different, less stable trajectory than the identical non-kk run; users following the doc's own example (line 37) get wrong results with no warning.
suggested_fix: Port the DLM branch into the kernel, or add 'if (dlm == DLM) error->all(FLERR,"Fix nve/sphere/kk does not (yet) support update dipole/dlm");' in FixNVESphereKokkos's constructor.

summary: FixNVESphereKokkos has no dlm handling at all: it only tests 'extra == DIPOLE', so 'fix nve/sphere/kk ... update dipole/dlm' silently uses the plain cross-product dipole integrator instead of the DLM integrator the CPU style selects.
verified_by: orchestrator (src/fix_nve_sphere.cpp:31/46/54-56 define and set dlm, :141-143 branch on it; grep 'dlm' over src/KOKKOS/fix_nve_sphere_kokkos.cpp returns nothing).

summary: restore_bias_all_kk() calls the internal temperature compute's host-syncing restore_bias_all() instead of restore_bias_all_kk(), forcing a full device-to-host copy of the velocities on every call.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/compute_temp_deform_kokkos.cpp:148-159 'void ComputeTempDeformKokkos<DeviceType>::restore_bias_all_kk() { if (which == BIAS) { if (temperature->kokkosable) temperature->restore_bias_all(); ...' versus the matching remove path at :123-134 'void ComputeTempDeformKokkos<DeviceType>::remove_bias_all_kk() { remove_deform_bias_all_kk(); if (which == BIAS) { if (temperature->kokkosable) temperature->remove_bias_all_kk();'. The _kk-suffixed variants exist precisely to skip the host round trip: e.g. src/KOKKOS/compute_temp_partial_kokkos.cpp:213-217 'void ComputeTempPartialKokkos<DeviceType>::restore_bias_all() { restore_bias_all_kk(); atomKK->sync(Host,V_MASK); }'.
failure_scenario: 'fix nvt/sllod/kk' with a biased internal temperature compute (src/KOKKOS/fix_nvt_sllod_kokkos.cpp:221 and src/KOKKOS/fix_nh_kokkos.cpp:558,716 drive these paths every timestep): each timestep pays an extra full v device->host transfer. Results are still correct.
suggested_fix: Call temperature->restore_bias_all_kk() in the kokkosable branch, mirroring remove_bias_all_kk().

summary: remove_deform_bias_all_kk() converts coordinates with DomainKokkos::x2lamda(), which always runs on the device and marks only the device copy modified, while the bias kernel of the LMPHostType instantiation reads the host x view - so 'compute temp/deform/kk/host' on a GPU build computes the bias from Cartesian instead of lamda coordinates.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/compute_temp_deform_kokkos.cpp:175-197: 'atomKK->sync(execution_space,X_MASK|V_MASK|MASK_MASK); ... x = atomKK->k_x.view<DeviceType>(); ... domainKK->x2lamda(nlocal); ... Kokkos::parallel_for(Kokkos::RangePolicy<DeviceType, TagComputeTempDeformRemoveBias>(0,nlocal),*this); ... domainKK->lamda2x(nlocal);' with no sync between x2lamda and the kernel. src/KOKKOS/domain_kokkos.cpp x2lamda(int n) is hard-wired to the device: 'atomKK->sync(Device,X_MASK); x = atomKK->k_x.view_device(); Kokkos::parallel_for(Kokkos::RangePolicy<LMPDeviceType, TagDomain_x2lamda>(0,n),*this); atomKK->modified(Device,X_MASK);' (detached_atom_x() is 0 in normal runs, src/KOKKOS/domain_kokkos.cpp:344-347). The style is instantiated for the host too: src/KOKKOS/compute_temp_deform_kokkos.h:18 'ComputeStyle(temp/deform/kk/host,ComputeTempDeformKokkos<LMPHostType>);' and src/KOKKOS/compute_temp_deform_kokkos.cpp:308. The CPU original computes lamda in a local temporary instead: src/compute_temp_deform.cpp:311-321 'domain->x2lamda(atom->x[i], lamda); vbiasall[i][0] = h_rate[0]*lamda[0] + ...'.
failure_scenario: GPU-enabled KOKKOS build + 'compute t all temp/deform/kk/host' (or fix nvt/sllod/kk whose temperature compute is a host-space temp/deform): the kernel at :205-207 uses x in box units (e.g. 0..Lx) where lamda units (0..1) are expected, so the removed streaming velocity is off by a factor of the box length and the reported temperature is wrong.
suggested_fix: After domainKK->x2lamda(nlocal), re-sync and re-fetch the view for the compute's execution space ('atomKK->sync(execution_space,X_MASK); x = atomKK->k_x.view<DeviceType>();'), or compute the lamda transform inline in the kernel from domain->h_inv/boxlo as the CPU style does.

summary: The KOKKOS bias removal round-trips every local atom's coordinates through x2lamda()/lamda2x(), perturbing atom->x by floating-point round-off, whereas the CPU style never modifies atom->x.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/compute_temp_deform_kokkos.cpp:186 'domainKK->x2lamda(nlocal);' and :195 'domainKK->lamda2x(nlocal);' bracket the bias kernel and operate on all nlocal atoms in place (both call atomKK->modified(Device,X_MASK)). The CPU original writes the transformed coordinates to a stack temporary and leaves atom->x untouched: src/compute_temp_deform.cpp:307-321 'double lamda[3]; ... domain->x2lamda(atom->x[i], lamda);'.
failure_scenario: 'fix nvt/sllod' + 'compute temp/deform/kk': coordinates of every atom (including atoms outside the compute group) are rewritten as lamda2x(x2lamda(x)) on every invocation, so trajectories drift from the CPU reference and depend on how often the compute is invoked (thermo frequency).
suggested_fix: Pass domain->h_inv/boxlo (or h/h_rate directly in lamda form) into the kernel and compute the lamda coordinates locally instead of transforming atom->x in place.

summary: norm_functor stores the FFT normalization factor in an 'int' member, so the 1/(nfast*nmid*nslow) scaling is truncated to 0 and a scaled backward FFT would zero the whole output array.
failure_scenario: Any FFT3dKokkos created with scaled=1 (the constructor argument) returns an all-zero backward transform.  Currently latent because the only in-tree caller, src/KOKKOS/pppm_kokkos.cpp:879-887, passes scaled=0 and does its own scaling; a new KOKKOS kspace style (or a fix to PPPM) that requests scaling silently gets zeros instead of an error.
suggested_fix: Change the functor member and constructor parameter to FFT_SCALAR (matching plan->norm / src/KSPACE/fft3d.cpp).

summary: The KISS FFT path allocates a fresh 'fft_3d:tmp' device view for each of the three 1d FFT stages on every fft_3d_kokkos() call instead of keeping a scratch view in the plan.
failure_scenario: KISS FFT is the default when no vendor FFT library is enabled; pppm/kk performs 4 FFTs per timestep, so this is 12 device allocate/free pairs per timestep, each of which serialises the device stream.
suggested_fix: Add a persistent tmp view to fft_plan_3d_kokkos (allocated once in fft_3d_create_plan_kokkos, sized like d_scratch) and reuse it in all three stages.

summary: d_num_ms_combs is allocated, only partially filled (rank-1 entries left uninitialized) and never read by any kernel.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/pair_pace_kokkos.cpp:647 allocates it, :699 fills it only for rank>1 functions ('h_num_ms_combs(mu, idx_func_through) = func->num_ms_combs;'), :724 deep-copies it; grep over pair_pace_kokkos.{cpp,h} shows no read other than memory_usage() at :3341. Identical dead array in pair_pace_extrapolation_kokkos.cpp:333/394/426.
failure_scenario: No wrong results; wasted device memory and an uninitialized-mirror read if a future change starts using it.
suggested_fix: Drop d_num_ms_combs (and its mirror/deep_copy) from both PACE KOKKOS styles.

summary: The per-atom core-repulsion factor is written into corerep_factor[] indexed by the neighbor-list position (chunk_offset+i) instead of by the atom index d_ilist[chunk_offset+i], unlike the CPU base which indexes by the atom i.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/pair_pace_kokkos.cpp:1223-1225: 'for (int i = 0; i < chunk_size; i++) corerep_factor[chunk_offset+i] = h_corerep(i);' while every kernel resolves the atom as 'const int i = d_ilist[ii + chunk_offset];' (e.g. compute_fs_one, line 2178). The CPU base src/ML-PACE/pair_pace.cpp:201-202 does 'i = list->ilist[ii]; ... corerep_factor[i] = 1 - aceimpl->ace->ace_fcut;'. Same pattern in src/KOKKOS/pair_pace_extrapolation_kokkos.cpp:811-821 for extrapolation_grade_gamma and corerep_factor.
failure_scenario: Whenever the KOKKOS neighbor list's ilist is not the identity permutation of 0..nlocal-1, 'compute pace/atom' (corerep factor / gamma grade) reports the values attached to the wrong atoms.
suggested_fix: Copy d_ilist to the host once per chunk and write corerep_factor[h_ilist(chunk_offset+i)] = h_corerep(i) (likewise for extrapolation_grade_gamma), matching the base class.

summary: The hard-core (core-repulsion) part of the pair force is added to f_ij without the 'scale' prefactor in both pace/kk and pace/extrapolation/kk, whereas the CPU base multiplies the complete neighbours_forces (which includes that term) by scale.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/pair_pace_kokkos.cpp:2856-2859 'const KK_FLOAT fpair = dF_drho_core(ii) * dcr(ii,jj); f_ij(ii, jj, 0) = scale * f_ji[0] + fpair * r_hat[0];' (and the ZBL term at :2865-2867 'f_ij(ii, jj, 0) += dF_dfcut(ii) * r_hat[0];' is also unscaled); identical code at src/KOKKOS/pair_pace_extrapolation_kokkos.cpp:1691-1702. The CPU base src/ML-PACE/pair_pace.cpp:212-214 applies the factor to the whole per-neighbor force: 'fij[0] = scale[itype][itype] * aceimpl->ace->neighbours_forces(jj, 0);'.
failure_scenario: With 'fix adapt pair pace scale * * v_s' and s != 1 on a potential that has a hard-core repulsion / ZBL inner cutoff, the /kk run scales only the basis part of the force while the CPU run scales everything, so the two diverge and the /kk forces are inconsistent with the (fully scaled) energy.
suggested_fix: Multiply the core-repulsion and dF_dfcut contributions by 'scale' as well: f_ij = scale * (f_ji + fpair*r_hat [+ dF_dfcut*r_hat]).

summary: improper distance/kk drops the five domain->minimum_image() calls that the CPU ImproperDistance::compute applies to every bond vector, so the /kk style computes a different plane normal and different forces whenever a bond vector is longer than half the box.
evidence: CPU src/EXTRA-MOLECULE/improper_distance.cpp:98-125 computes each of the five vectors and immediately folds it: `xab = x[i2][0] - x[i1][0]; ... domain->minimum_image(FLERR, xab,yab,zab);` (also for xac/yac/zac :107, xad/yad/zad :113, xbc/ybc/zbc :119, xbd/ybd/zbd :125). The KOKKOS kernel src/KOKKOS/improper_distance_kokkos.cpp:149-167 computes exactly the same five differences and never folds any of them: `const KK_FLOAT xab = x(i2,0) - x(i1,0); ... const KK_FLOAT zbd = x(i4,2) - x(i2,2);` -- there is no minimum-image code anywhere in the file (`grep -n minimum_image src/KOKKOS/improper_distance_kokkos.cpp` is empty) and domain.h is not even included. The KOKKOS package already has a device-side implementation of this that could be reused: BondHarmonicRestrainKokkos copies domain->xprd/xprd_half/triclinic in compute() (src/KOKKOS/bond_harmonic_restrain_kokkos.cpp:111-121) and calls its own KOKKOS_INLINE_FUNCTION minimum_image() (:191, defined :243-295).
failure_scenario: A periodic cell whose shortest edge is less than twice an improper bond length (small unit cells, or an improper spanning a periodic image), run with improper_style distance vs distance/kk: the CPU style folds e.g. xbd back into the box before forming the plane normal, the /kk style does not, so the normal, the projection da, the energy k*da^2+chi*da^4 and all four forces differ.
suggested_fix: Copy domain->triclinic/xprd/yprd/zprd/*_half into the functor in compute() and add a KOKKOS_INLINE_FUNCTION minimum_image() applied to the five difference vectors, mirroring src/KOKKOS/bond_harmonic_restrain_kokkos.cpp:243-295.

summary: The KOKKOS M-site pre-kernel drops the CPU styles' check that the two atoms found by tag+1/tag+2 really are of type typeH, so a mis-ordered water topology silently produces wrong M sites instead of an error.
failure_scenario: A data file where an O atom's tag+1 / tag+2 are not its two H atoms (e.g. water mixed with other molecules, or ions numbered between the water atoms): tip4p/cut and tip4p/long abort with a clear error, tip4p/cut/kk and tip4p/long/kk build M sites from the wrong atoms and silently return wrong forces and energies.
suggested_fix: In the TagPairTIP4PNewsite kernel, also set d_hneigh(i,0) = -1 (or a separate error flag) when type(iH1) != m_typeH || type(iH2) != m_typeH, and report the distinct 'incorrect atom type' error from finalize().

summary: NBinKokkos::c_bincount is declared const and is never initialized (so it is permanently an empty view and makes the class non-copy-assignable), and c_bins is assigned only on a regrow and never read.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/nbin_kokkos.h:51 'const typename AT::t_int_1d_const c_bincount;' and :53 'typename AT::t_int_2d_const c_bins;'.  c_bins is written once at src/KOKKOS/nbin_kokkos.cpp:157 'c_bins = bins;' and neither member is read anywhere: the consumers use their own copies, see src/KOKKOS/npair_kokkos.h:220-222 and :316 'bincount(_bincount),c_bincount(_bincount),bins(_bins),c_bins(_bins),' fed from src/KOKKOS/npair_kokkos.cpp:104-105 'k_bincount = nbKK->k_bincount; k_bins = nbKK->k_bins;'.
failure_scenario: No runtime effect today; the const member silently deletes NBinKokkos's copy-assignment operator, so any future code that assigns one of these objects fails to compile for a non-obvious reason.
suggested_fix: Delete both members (or, if they are meant to be used, drop the const qualifier and assign them wherever bins/bincount are refreshed, including NBinKokkos::bin_atoms_setup).

summary: The neighbor-list error message in dihedral charmmfsw/kk names the wrong style ('charmm/kk'), which will misdirect a user who is running charmmfsw/kk.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/dihedral_charmmfsw_kokkos.cpp:83-84 'if (lmp->kokkos->neighflag == FULL)\n    error->all(FLERR,"Dihedral_style charmm/kk requires half neighbor list");' -- copy-pasted verbatim from src/KOKKOS/dihedral_charmm_kokkos.cpp:76-77 without renaming the style.
failure_scenario: User runs 'dihedral_style charmmfsw/kk' with '-pk kokkos neigh full' and is told that 'Dihedral_style charmm/kk' is at fault, a style not present in the input.
suggested_fix: Change the message text to 'Dihedral_style charmmfsw/kk requires half neighbor list'.

summary: For special-bonded pairs the CPU core/shell style rescales the WHOLE pair force (Coulomb and Born) by 1/(rsq+EPS_EWALD_SQR), but the KOKKOS split into compute_fcoul/compute_fpair applies that rescaling only to the Coulomb part, leaving the Born part scaled by 1/rsq.
evidence:
src/CORESHELL/pair_born_coul_long_cs.cpp:113-126 sets `r2inv = 1.0/(rsq + EPS_EWALD_SQR);` inside the `factor_coul < 1.0` branch, and that same r2inv is then used for the Born term at :154 `r6inv = r2inv*r2inv*r2inv;` / :157 and for the combined scaling at :160 `fpair = (forcecoul + factor_lj*forceborn) * r2inv;`.
src/KOKKOS/pair_born_coul_long_cs_kokkos.cpp:264 `return forcecoul / (rsq_cs + static_cast<KK_FLOAT>(EPS_EWALD_SQR));` (Coulomb only), while :185-215 compute_fpair uses `rsq = rsq_in + EPSILON; r2inv = 1.0/rsq; ... return forceborn*r2inv;` with no EPS_EWALD_SQR, and pair_kokkos.h:245-248 just adds the two contributions.
failure_scenario: A special-bonded (factor_coul < 1) core/shell pair that is also inside cut_lj gets a Born force differing from the CPU style by a relative 1e-12/rsq; visible as a small mismatch in a tight force-style regression comparison against the CPU reference.
suggested_fix: Either apply the EPS_EWALD_SQR-corrected inverse-square scaling to the Born term too (e.g. pass factor_coul into compute_fpair), or document the intentional deviation.

summary: The KOKKOS integrate style verlet/kk is completely undocumented: doc/src/run_style.rst has no verlet/kk in its style list, no '.. index:: run_style verlet/kk', no 'Accelerator Variant' line and no '.. include:: accel_styles.rst'.
failure_scenario: A KOKKOS user who wants to select the integrator explicitly (e.g. 'run_style verlet/kk' when not using -suffix kk) finds no documentation that the style exists or what it does differently; conversely a reader of run_style.rst believes the KOKKOS package does not accelerate the integrator at all.
suggested_fix: Add *verlet/kk* to the style list on doc/src/run_style.rst:13, add '.. index:: run_style verlet/kk', an 'Accelerator Variant: *verlet/kk*' line after the title and '.. include:: accel_styles.rst' near the end of the page.
